subject: Follow-up: cost levers and capacity constraints from today's call
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: cost levers and capacity constraints from today's call

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we agreed on so nothing falls through the cracks. I captured the cost/TCO levers we discussed and a rough framing for a small pilot to validate throughput and token economics.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- High peak latency during end-of-day reconciliation jobs (95th pct spikes to ~1.2s/token) — impacts customer SLAs
- Token burn risk from high-parallel chat workloads; forecasted 2.5x multiplier on production traffic
- Procurement/budget window: Q4 cap on new vendor spend with a target payback within 3–6 months

Goals from our side:
1) Reduce per-token cost through batching + prefix (KV) cache while keeping p95 latency < 350ms for interactive flows.
2) Scope a 6-week pilot that shows savings/latency tradeoffs and an ROI projection suitable for your procurement team.
3) Identify committed capacity or reserved path if the ROI works out (savings share vs monthly commit).

TCO levers we recommended (high-level):
- Continuous batching: expected 20–35% token-cost reduction for async reconciliation; depends on latency SLOs.
- KV/prefix caching for recurring prompts: up to 40% fewer model calls on stable flows.
- Quantized model variant for non-customer-facing inference: 10–25% GPU cost reduction with minor quality checks.
- Smart routing: route low-priority/async requests to lower-cost instances to protect p95 for interactive flows.

Very rough back-of-envelope (today's numbers):
- Current baseline: ~1.8M tokens/day, avg cost $0.0009/token => ~$1,620/day
- Target with levers (pilot): 30–45% unit-cost reduction => ~$890–1,130/day (savings ~$15k–18k/month)

Attachments: short brief with assumptions and a sample ROI sheet [Attachment: redwood-token-econ-brief.pdf (2 pages)]

Proposed next steps (please confirm priorities):
- Elena/Team: confirm which workload(s) to include in pilot (chat front-end + nightly reconciliation were discussed).
- Redwood: share a pilot TCO spreadsheet and a short ops checklist for instrumentation (I attached an editable version in the follow-up).
- Schedule: technical deep-dive + infra checklist next week (30–45 min).

If this matches your view I can: 1) prepare two pilot scenarios (conservative / aggressive savings) and 2) loop Ben to propose an economical commit option we can present to procurement.

Thanks — feel free to correct any details I missed.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122

[Attachment: redwood-token-econ-brief.pdf]

From: Elena Morales <elena@fastledger.com>

Cc: Rajiv Patel <raj@fastledger.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: cost levers and capacity constraints from today's call

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear recap. This aligns well. A few clarifications from our side before we lock pilot scope:

1) Volume & windows: the reconciliation job is the big cost driver — runs between 02:00–06:00 PT and is extremely latency tolerant, so batching there makes sense. The chat front-end is the priority for p95 improvement.

2) Budget constraint: procurement has authorized a single vendor pilot up to $25k total for Q4. We need to show a path to break-even inside that envelope.

3) Data residency: any logs or KV caching must remain inside our GCP project and be covered by your SOC2 scope. Marissa — can you confirm the caching architecture and where keys live?

4) Timing: next-week tech deep-dive works for us on Thu 11/12 or Fri 11/13 afternoon PT.

If you can send the conservative/aggressive scenarios and the editable spreadsheet, I’ll loop Raj (CTO) and procurement to get alignment.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Engineering, FastLedger
elena@fastledger.com | +1 (617) 555-1983

Elena —

Thanks — noted on the $25k pilot cap and the windows. Attached is a lightweight TCO workbook with two scenarios (conservative / aggressive) that map the levers we discussed to expected monthly spend and estimated payback. I called out the assumptions in the Overview tab.

Pilot proposal (6 weeks):
- Week 0: instrumentation & SLA definition (hooks for prefix cache metrics, token counts, p95 latency).
- Weeks 1–3: run pilot on a mirror of the reconciliation job + shadow chat traffic (no customer-facing change).
- Weeks 4–6: enable live batching and KV cache for the reconciliation job; enable cautious quantized variant on a subset of async flows. Monitor quality and p95.

Estimated cost & savings (scenario highlights from the sheet):
- Conservative: 22% unit-cost reduction, pilot spend ~$18k, projected monthly savings post-pilot ~$7k
- Aggressive: 40% unit-cost reduction, pilot spend ~$24k, projected monthly savings post-pilot ~$18k

I attached the workbook: fastledger-tco-scenarios.xlsx (editable). Please review assumptions (notably baseline token burn) and I’ll update with your telemetry once we have access.

Proposed times for technical deep-dive: Thu 11/12 11:00–11:45 PT or Fri 11/13 14:00–14:45 PT. Which works better?

Ben — looping you in to help draft a short commitment/discount structure that fits their $25k pilot cap and shows an attractive ROI if they choose reserved capacity after the pilot.

Jordan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
